full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah, J: This Criminal Revisional application at the instance of Mohammad Ali under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 and mad with section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is directed against the order No. 72 dated 24.06.2004 passed by the learned Special Judge, Mymensingh in Special Case No. 97 of 2001 arising out of Kamalkanda P.S Case No. 4 dated 27.02.1994 under section 409/477A of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act of 1947 for splitting up the case as per law. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the petitioner is a Tahsildar, in charge of Langua Union Tahsil office of Kamalkanda police station under Netrokona District and during the period from 30.06.1988 to 30.06.1991, he in the capacity of public officer (Government employee) realized land development tax through 26 numbers of receipts (Dakhilas) Taka 1,27,383.80 but he deposited in the government account only Taka 281.18 and thereby for illegal gain, he misappropriated Taka 1,27,102/- and for this misappropriation he adopted policy that he did not use carbon paper to issue the rent receipts. In the original rent receipt (Dakhila), he wrote quantum of land more tax accordingly but in the duplicate he wrote less quantum of land and tax less accordingly. Thus he committed the offence punishable under section 409/420/477A of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Act II of 1947. 

 4. The case was investigated by the District Anti-Corruption Bureau and during investigation, the investigating officer examined witnesses, seized alamats and after the close of investigation, he submitted charge sheet No.47 dated 30.04.1994 against the petitioner for the offence punishable under section 409/420/477A of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Act II of 1947 for misappropriation of Taka 1,34,144.88 against 35 numbers of dakhilas by which he realised Taka 1,34,587.98 out of which he deposited to government account Taka 443.10 only. 

 9. Mr. Mizanur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the case is triable as per Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure are applicable so far the provisions which are not inconsistent with the provisions contained in section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act. He refers section 6 (1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act which reads as follows: 

 14. There is no denying of the fact that the charges were framed against the accused petitioner on 20.02.2001 under section 409/477A of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.1947. These sections clearly fall under the schedule of Criminal Law Amendment Act,1958 which will be tried by the Special Judge. 

 "6(1B) A person accused of more offences than one punishable under this act may be tried at one trial for all such offences." Since section 409/477 A read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act fall under schedule of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, so the offence under these sections will be tried as per the provision of the Criminal Law Amendment Act. The Criminal Law Amendment Act is a Special Law and this law will prevail over the general law like Code of Criminal Procedure. Since sections 409/477A read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 fall under the schedule of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, so these sections will be tried as per the provision of Criminal Law Amendment Act. 

 18. It may be mentioned here that when the charge of this case was framed on 20.02.2001 under section 409 of the Penal Code, then section 409 was under schedule of Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and later on section 408 was replaced instead of section 409.
